speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and was there any specific injury or event that preceded it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. I understand this occurred during a football game when your finger was pulled.

Can you tell me if you are able to fully straighten the tip of your finger, and does it feel unstable or like it is catching?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. You must output exactly the following diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyelonephritis

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mechanism of injury and your symptoms—specifically the inability to flex the fingertip and the finger resting in extension—are classic signs of a "Jersey Finger," which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon.

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand

Can you confirm if you can actively flex just the very tip of your finger while keeping the middle joint straight?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The X-ray confirms there are no fractures, which supports a tendon injury diagnosis given the mechanism and symptoms.

To differentiate between a Jersey finger and a Mallet finger, can you tell me if you have difficulty actively extending the tip of the finger, or is the issue strictly with flexion?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint following a forced extension injury is pathognomonic for a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion, commonly known as Jersey finger. The negative X-ray rules out bony avulsion fractures, pointing to a soft tissue tendon rupture.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
